approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It samples breeding parents from high-scoring population quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover or successive local atom and bond edits, and fills a fresh surplus pool after graph validation, stable canonical identity checks and duplicate rejection. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted archive uses integer-count Morgan features and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Correlated function draws choose distinct pool members for evaluation; real accepted scores then update the archive and a bounded score-greedy population.
approach.novelty: Remove the composite posterior selector's influence on successful emissions: take the first announced batch of valid unique pool members in generation order. Keep the complete inherited pool, model fitting, full covariance and original draws as passive controls. Earlier siblings removed counts, sampled residuals or their correlation while retaining predictive allocation. This test instead removes all predictive ranking at once at the existing pool boundary, treating the selector as one module. The independent sampled comparator records which identities would differ on each actual pool; it supplies no scores for unevaluated alternatives.

observed_bottleneck: The unresolved behavior in n-62daf219c70a is active predictive allocation from an expensive complete fresh graph pool without an isolated current-Parent contrast against generation-order allocation at the same effort. The actual three summary.json/run.log pairs are complete: macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. Reading all fifteen task logs reconstructs 435 full 160-member pools, 69600 pool admissions, 4350 masked sampled maxima and 65250 earlier accepted training-row occurrences. All 435 selected sets differ from their own pool's first ten members; 4066 emitted identities lie outside that prefix, 4317 ordered positions differ, and total set overlap is 284 of 4350. On the generation-order available masks, the same recorded function rows strictly prefer another member in 4318 positions. All 435 pools have nonzero off-diagonal covariance, and all 870 factorizations succeed at the first jitter; no numerical fallback or truncated pool is observed. These are real allocation opportunities, not evidence for the scores of unselected prefixes. The historical composite addition n-fc2c108a5253 enlarged the pool and added the selector together under a binary representation and has only one matched direct-Parent seed; its +0.05588031291682699 screening delta cannot answer this test. Current component removals n-299096e31fe7, n-54adc6a641e8 and n-e00db808bbb4 lose matched mean 0.07686116167690966, 0.018447481386582327 and 0.051295849138213355 respectively, while preserving task-seed gains and, for correlation removal, a +0.03550275965606198 seed-macro gain. They retain other predictive channels and do not establish the composite contrast or an additive prediction.
hypothesis: Remove all posterior-based influence on successful offspring allocation by selecting the first announced-batch-size valid unique candidates in inherited generation order from the fully generated pool, while retaining the complete accepted-only posterior computation and original draws passively.

finding_summary.headline: Generation-order allocation loses 0.124388 in mean endpoint score despite retaining full pool and model effort.
finding_summary.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 successful batches evaluated the first ten members of a completed 160-member pool, with zero prefix-order violations or choices outside that prefix. The passive original sampler selected a different set in all 435 batches, and its sampled values strictly preferred another candidate on 4,317 of 4,350 generation-order masks. Thus the removal changed real evaluation choices under strong exposure. All 435 fits, full covariance factorizations and original normal arrays remained computed; the accepted-only feedback and identity-bound prediction joins passed. No natural numerical fallback or incomplete pool occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.471282, a paired change of -0.124388, well beyond the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.134968, -0.105769 and -0.132426. All five task means declined. Thirteen of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined; zaleplon_mpo seeds zero and one improved by 0.019694 and 0.005802. Macro population deviation changed from 0.026593 to 0.014583. Correct removal and the predicted score loss support positive contribution from the composite selector in this exact full-pool search loop.

molecular.headline: Aromatic families remain, with useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives alongside peroxides, O-halogen bonds and difficult rings
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-01b48dd09404 and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were read, with no missing paths or uncovered objectives. The brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatches. Each task has 900 Child trajectory records, including 870 optimizer records, and a complete matched Parent panel. The fixed initial molecules and their scores match within each paired task/seed. These trajectories describe accepted evaluated molecules; they do not enumerate every valid pool member, unselected candidate or rejected graph. The digest field proposed_by_optimizer and all chemistry frequencies below therefore concern recorded optimizer evaluations, not a census of the complete inherited generation pool. An emitted molecule, an accepted evaluation, and the highest observed retained endpoint are different observations. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 evaluations, not every seed's retained incumbent; full trajectories supply the endpoint comparisons. The registered contrast removes posterior influence on successful allocation at full inherited pool effort while retaining posterior computation passively. This report does not audit activation, describe deletion of the optimizer, attribute chemistry to an individual posterior component, or infer pool reduction or compute savings. The output contains indole amides and ketones, nitrile-bearing biaryl amines attached to unsaturated ether/peroxide rings, linked aza-aromatic carbonyl systems, aryl tertiary amines, fused nitrogen diones, and both fluorinated aza-aromatics and densely oxygenated nonaromatic cages. Child ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9598, 0.9724, 0.9805, 0.9448 and 0.9437 in fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9506, 0.9701, 0.9563, 0.9402 and 0.6609. These measure feature presence in molecular strings, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. The final stream includes a wholly nonaromatic seed family, so aromatic richness is not universal within every seed. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. Available aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres remain plainly present. Read-only RDKit perception of the exact trajectory graphs supports size, ring and functional-group descriptions; no new objective, affinity, feasibility or synthesis scores were calculated. The overall chemistry remains questionable in synthetic plausibility and weak in drug-likeness, with ordinary medicinal functional groups mixed with O-F/O-Cl bonds, peroxides, acyl fluoride, unusual carbon-sulfur triple bonds, strained unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry. The relatively conventional tertiary-amine ketone and successful carbonyl-free nitrile family are important counterexamples: neither reactive bonds nor the Parent's exact scaffold families are universal necessities. Across-seed structural diversity is moderate, with narrower related series among each seed's leaders. No general absence of rings, amines or scaffold alternatives is demonstrated, especially in the unobserved pool. The original n-c55c3d520a2c report and its carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh evidence index. The transferable gaps retain that provenance and are re-observed here under the current complete matched conditions; historical origin is not extra replication. Only Child SMILES from the digest or the trusted citation_trajectory_paths are quoted. Parent-only structures are described by published task/seed/evaluation. Read-only evidence and descriptors are in .slots/r0017-02-ablation-L01/molecular/trajectory_audit.json and inspected_records.json; history_molecular_sources.json preserves the original reports and source hashes. No structural association below assigns a reward to an unselected pool molecule or establishes which chemical change mediated the endpoint contrast.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader (evaluation 203) is a compact nitrile-bearing phenyl/pyridyl system connected through an NH group to an unsaturated oxygen ring containing an O-O bond and a fluoroethyl side chain. Related high-scoring members instead have a cyclic ether without peroxide. This family contains no carbonyl and no N-halogen bond. Seed 0 reaches a fused/bridged indole carboxanilide with methoxy, methyl and ordinary aryl fluorine substitution; seed 2 reaches an indole-linked aryl ketone with an additional O-CH2-N-containing ring. These leading molecules are compact, ring-rich and substantially aromatic. Mean Child SMILES length is 45.4, with a maximum of 95 and halogen-string incidence of 0.7609. The Parent leaders are an amino-substituted cumulene on an N-chloro indole (seed 0, evaluation 289), an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide with N-F (seed 1, 293), and an N-chloro indole vicinal diketone (seed 2, 294). The Child reaches higher retained endpoints in seeds 0 and 1 and a lower endpoint in seed 2, while avoiding N-halogen bonds in all these cited Child leaders. That is heterogeneous chemical change, not a uniform loss of useful chemistry.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader contains an O-O bond in an unsaturated ring. Its supplied score does not demonstrate stability or make the peroxide necessary; a cyclic ether relative also scores highly.

The other leaders have unusual fused/bridged connectivity or an O-CH2-N local environment and no stereochemical specification. Their conventional amide, ketone and aryl fluorine groups do not certify a route for the entire graph.
Very small fragments and much larger joined structures can both have negligible scores; molecular size is not a sufficient chemical quality rule.
missing_features: Consistent conventional alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/polar organization are not established throughout the evaluated stream; the nonperoxide cyclic ether is already accessible and useful, so peroxide chemistry is not an unavoidable limitation.
Defined stereochemistry and conformational identity are absent for the fused/bridged saturated centres, while the unsaturated peroxide ring requires a distinct stability assessment.

The trajectory does not reveal an exact absent target pharmacophore. Both carbonyl-bearing and carbonyl-free leading frameworks exist, so the missing capability is reliable feasible alternatives rather than a prescribed carbonyl motif.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leaders are medium-sized linked pyrrole/pyrimidine/aniline systems with an N-methyl diacyl group, an imine-containing side chain, an aryl chloride and a peroxide-bearing vinyl substituent. Some relatives replace an acetyl group with a carbonyl fluoride or replace the peroxide-containing appendage by an imine/acetal-like group. Seed 1 produces a more compact linked azaaryl amine/carboxamide carrying methylthio, ordinary aryl fluorines and O-Cl substitution. Seed 0 instead reaches a substantially larger polyheteroaromatic carbonyl assembly with a heavily halogenated ether, O-Cl and very small aromatic-labelled ring circuits. Mean Child SMILES length is 84.4 and the maximum is 225; larger evaluated structures coexist with the medium-sized seed-2 leaders. The Parent seed-0 leader (evaluation 281) is a much more compact linked aza-aromatic carbonyl-thione framework, while its seed-1 and seed-2 leaders (296 in both cases) are different linked heterocyclic families. All matched Child retained scores are lower, but seed 2 is close to its Parent despite its different chemistry; seed 0 is the strongest change in the cited endpoint comparison. The Parent compact leader itself has O-F and halomethyl-ether concerns, so its larger score is not a synthesis endorsement.
liabilities: Peroxide and hydroperoxide substituents, O-Cl bonds and carbonyl fluoride appear in useful-scoring structures; these differ chemically from ordinary ethers and aryl halides.

The large seed-0 leader combines dense heteroaromatic connectivity, small aromatic-labelled ring circuits, multiple carbonyls and a heavily halogenated ether. A valid aromatic graph does not establish a feasible geometry or preparation.
The imine-containing side chains and N-diacyl environments require local stability and tautomer assessment. The score ties do not validate any of those functional groups.
missing_features: The evaluated Child leading set does not recover the compact Parent seed-0 heterocyclic organization. This is a coverage observation about retained evaluated leaders, not proof that the inherited pool could not contain comparable chemistry.

Stable local substitutions preserving the favorable linked aromatic/amide arrangement are not consistently represented among leaders; the acetyl/carbonyl-fluoride tie and useful nonperoxide alternative show that some conventional options are available.

Reliable control of redundant elaboration and difficult small-ring connectivity is absent from the larger evaluated assemblies, without evidence that a universal size limit would improve the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (evaluation 254) is a comparatively conventional tertiary-amine ketone: propyl and fluoropropyl substituents on nitrogen, a ketone-containing chain to an indane, and a fluorinated methoxyphenyl substituent. It contains available aliphatic amine chemistry and ordinary carbon-bound fluorine, with no N-halogen, O-halogen or peroxide bond. A related high-scoring family uses an N-propyl piperidine instead. Seed 1 instead reaches a hydrophobic biaryl/azabicyclic system with a bromomethyl group and a benzylic chloride. Seed 2 retains larger phenolic biaryl/chroman systems connected through a diaminoalkene-like unit to an amino-substituted pyrrolidine bearing an aryl sulfone. Basic centres are therefore not missing globally, but their environments and surrounding scaffold differ considerably between seeds. Mean Child SMILES length is 70.1, maximum 220, and halogen-string incidence 0.9632. Parent leaders are a flexible aryl tertiary amine (seed 0, evaluation 284), an aminoalkyl pyrrolidine/aryl ether (seed 1, 261), and a pyrrolidine/fused thioether/biaryl framework (seed 2, 241). The Child seed-0 leader is chemically recognizable and retains a high supplied score, whereas the other Child seeds remain in different lower-scoring families. Neither more heteroatoms nor more rings consistently restores the Parent pattern.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader contains bromomethyl and benzylic chloride groups, a very hydrophobic aryl arrangement and a small fused nitrogen ring; these require local reactivity and geometry assessment.

The seed-2 leaders combine multiple polar and basic environments, an unsaturated diamino linkage, chloromethyl substitution and large aromatic surface. Late elaboration can add O-Cl or peroxide chemistry and substantial bulk.

The relatively conventional seed-0 amine/ketone is a counterexample to universal instability, but flexibility and unassigned stereochemistry still leave conformation, exposure and synthesis unverified.
missing_features: Consistent access across evaluated seed streams to conventional, available aliphatic amines in a useful aromatic arrangement is not demonstrated; the seed-0 leader proves the generator can already produce such chemistry.
Stereochemical identity of indane, benzylic and cyclic-amine centres is unspecified. Neutral strings also leave protonation unresolved, without implying an absence of basic sites.
Conventional replacements for bromomethyl/benzylic chloride and the crowded diaminoalkene/sulfone arrangement are not established at those seed endpoints; simply adding more amines is not supported.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (evaluation 265) is a diaryl fused nitrogen dione with N-methyl groups, an exocyclic amine, an ethoxy substituent and a pendant oxetane. Seed 1 reaches a partially saturated nitrogen dione attached to aryl groups, with a benzene-spanning oxygen-containing bridge and an unsaturated four-membered nitrogen ring fused to a larger carbonyl ring. Seed 2 reaches a propoxy diaryl nitrogen dicarbonyl system with chlorinated aryl groups and an N-N/imino segment. These are medium-sized aromatic/carbonyl frameworks with varied saturated-ring content. Mean Child SMILES length is 57.5 and halogen-string incidence 0.3149. The Parent leaders also join aromatic regions to nitrogen/carbonyl rings, including a diaryl N-O-containing bridged framework (seed 0, evaluation 293) and quinoline-linked dicarbonyl families (seeds 1 and 2, 278 and 261). All matched Child retained endpoints are lower, but the functional-group classes themselves are present. The difference is therefore not adequately described as absence of carbonyls, aromatic rings or nitrogen heterocycles.
liabilities: An isolated oxetane is recognizable synthetic chemistry; it must be distinguished from the seed-1 unsaturated four-membered nitrogen ring and crowded bridge topology, which raise different geometric concerns.
N-N/imino and occasional N-O connections vary across the families and require local assessment. They are not shared requirements of all leading examples.
The substituted saturated centres are unspecified, and the large joined relatives show that syntactic novelty can add complexity without preserving the useful score range.
missing_features: The evaluated leaders do not establish a reliably accessible alternative arrangement of the already-present aromatic and nitrogen/dicarbonyl features. An exact missing target motif cannot be inferred from these scalar scores.
Defined geometry and stereochemistry are missing for bridged centres and the small unsaturated nitrogen-ring junctions.
Chemically independent useful alternatives within a seed remain limited among the leaders, despite different families across seeds and an oxetane-containing leader with no N-N bond.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader (evaluation 165) is a compact linked pyridyl/fused nitrogen-dione system with N-methyl groups, a thiolmethyl substituent, ordinary aryl and alkyl fluorine, and an O-F bond. Nearby relatives include carbon-sulfur triple bonds ending in S-H or S-Cl, which must not be mistaken for ordinary nitriles or thioethers. Seed 0 instead retains a compact partly unsaturated nitrogen/carbonyl framework with hydroxylated substituents and a small imine ring, without halogens. Seed 1 remains in a wholly nonaromatic, densely bridged acetal-like N/O/S cage, including a three-membered O-C-S ring, an unsaturated four-membered oxygen ring and N-O links. Mean Child SMILES length is 47.2 and aromatic-string incidence only 0.6609; the nonaromatic seed family is a material exception to the other tasks' predominantly aromatic output. Geometric, tautomeric and stereochemical identity is unresolved for the bridged N/O/S cages and partially unsaturated nitrogen rings. The records do not identify an exact absent target-specific pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The general concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. This re-observation is n-01b48dd09404 versus that published Parent on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. Its registered condition is removal of posterior influence on successful allocation while retaining full inherited pool generation and passive posterior computation. The chemistry evidence covers accepted evaluations and their retained best values, not all unselected pool members; historical origin is not extra replication. Useful-scoring examples contain cyclic or pendant peroxides, O-Cl/O-F, carbonyl fluoride, bromomethyl/benzylic chloride, and unusual carbon-sulfur triple bonds with additional sulfur substitution. The sulfur environments are a current extension of the original local-reactivity concern. Counterexamples include a conventional flexible tertiary-amine ketone, a nonperoxide cyclic ether in a successful nitrile series, and identical scores for acetyl and carbonyl-fluoride relatives. Conversely, one close scaffold pair associates removal of O-F with a substantial score reduction, so the record does not show that conventional replacement always improves reward.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments in the molecular material that reaches evaluation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bond-environment-aware transformations and plausible alternatives that preserve useful functional relationships learned from current task-local feedback. Differentiate ordinary carbon-bound halogens and available amines from reactive heteroatom-halogen or unconventional sulfur environments. A blanket chemical filter, universal score benefit, absence of safer alternatives from the unobserved pool, or attribution to any posterior subcomponent does not follow.

Perceived aromaticity and ring count are not geometric evidence. Tiny halogens, hydrocarbons and simple heteroatom fragments appear at low values, including late evaluations. Large joined aromatic/dione and aryl-amine structures can also score far below their more compact relatives, while linked medium-sized heterocycles and a comparatively conventional flexible amine remain useful. A carbonyl-free nitrile family succeeds, showing that preserving context cannot mean requiring the Parent's exact carbonyl scaffold. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful molecular context while controlling fragmentation and excessive elaboration among evaluated proposals.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to preserve informative combinations of molecular regions while permitting simplification and scaffold replacement. Avoid turning a recurring functional group into a mandatory template or a size statistic into a fixed cutoff. The evaluated distribution cannot establish whether the full pool lacked better-sized alternatives, nor imply smaller pools, reduced generation effort, compute savings or a guaranteed score improvement.

Some streams remain among closely related halogen placements, short side chains or ring closures, and a compact Parent heterocyclic family is absent from the corresponding Child leading set. A current carbonyl-free nitrile family and a fused carboxanilide each exceed their matched Parent endpoint, and the flexible amine/ketone stream remains useful. transferable_gaps.gap: Plausible useful scaffold alternatives are not consistently represented across evaluated seed streams, despite genuine successful changes of scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support feasible scaffold transformations that preserve or replace useful functional relationships learned from feedback, and judge their evaluated descendants rather than counting new strings alone. Use successes outside inherited scaffold families to constrain any proposed chemistry rule. This conditional coverage concern does not show which posterior component supplied useful allocation, label unselected molecules with rewards, attribute the outcome to pool effort, or establish that more diversity alone raises the endpoint.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
